title: MCP with LangChain & LangGraph
summary: The client side: LangChain and LangGraph apps that use MCP servers. MCPAdapter turns server tools into LangChain tools. Apps read prompts and resources (always-on context, or loaded per request in a graph). Many servers sit behind one agent without name clashes. People approve what the server marks destructive, and answer what a server asks mid-call. Connections are kept open and tool lists cached. Agents are served as MCP tools in turn. The product gets a support agent that is purely an MCP client: its tools, its policy and its approval rules all come from the Nimbus server.
learn: **MCPAdapter**: MCP tools as LangChain tools, called directly or by agents and graphs (async)
**Prompts and resources in apps**: prompts for any model, resources as always-on or per-request context, ResourcesAsTools
**Many servers**: MCPConfig with prefixed names and mixed transports, ClientGroup
**Humans in the loop**: approvals from annotations, elicitation as interrupts
**Connections and caching**, and **agents served over MCP** (including LangGraph Server's /mcp)
flow:
support agent (create_agent) ── MCPAdapter ──→ Nimbus server
  tools        ← list_tools()                          (support_* through the gateway)
  policy       ← read_resource(policies/refunds) on every model call
  approvals    ← tools the server marks destructiveHint → HumanInTheLoopMiddleware
  questions    ← elicitation → LangGraph interrupt → the customer answers → resume

labs.explain:
The Nimbus server over **stdio** through **MCPAdapter**: its tools as StructuredTools with **annotations**, called directly (content blocks, a ToolMessage with an **artifact**, an error), **async only**, and used by **create_agent** and a hand-built **ToolNode** graph.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The **support_reply** prompt run by a LangChain model, the refund policy as **always-on context**, a LangGraph node that **loads resources** per request, and **ResourcesAsTools**. The graph's answer misread 'processing' as 'packed': read the outputs.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

A café server and a roastery server that both offer **price**: stdio and HTTP in one **MCPConfig** (prefixed names), an agent choosing correctly, and a **ClientGroup** with one connection per server (one pinned to the legacy era).

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

cancel_order **pauses for approval** because the server marks it destructive, then the server **asks the customer** to confirm (an interrupt); approved and rejected. Then a booking whose two questions become interrupts.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Calls with the adapter **closed** (17 ms each: a connection per call) and **open** (3 ms), **parallel** calls on one connection, and **tool-list caching** with the server's freshness hints.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The Nimbus assistant as **one MCP tool** (ask_nimbus), used by a concierge agent (**agent-to-agent**); then **LangGraph Server's /mcp**, where every hosted graph is a tool with its input and output schemas as the interface.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

path.title: Production path: the support agent as an MCP client
path.summary: The support agent connects to the Nimbus gateway and keeps no business knowledge of its own. Tools come from list_tools. The refund policy is a resource read into the system prompt on every model call, so a policy change reaches every agent without a redeploy. Approvals cover whatever tools the server marks destructive, and the server's mid-call questions pause the agent for the customer.

steps.title: Agent
steps.explain: build_mcp_agent reads tools, the policy and the approval rules from the server. The dynamic_prompt middleware fetches the policy fresh; the HumanInTheLoopMiddleware `when` predicate checks destructiveHint.
production: Keep business rules on the server: every agent and host that connects gets the same ones.

steps.title: Serve
steps.explain: ask_nimbus wraps the router assistant as one MCP tool; server/assistant_graph.py exposes it through LangGraph Server's /mcp with question and customer_id in, answer out.
production: The customer id is an argument for now; MCP Module 4 takes it from the caller's token.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
LangChain Module 3's 12 tool requests plus MCP Module 2's 8 policy questions, through an agent on the server's tools alone and through the production MCP agent.

| | success | right facts | model calls | tokens | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MCP tools only (Module 1) | 12/20 | 0.60 | 1.70 | 1,418 | 4.8 s |
| **MCP agent: tools + live policy + approvals** | **19/20** | **1.00** | **1.65** | **1,552** | **4.9 s** |

Tools alone missed 7 of the 8 policy questions: it invented a "3–5 business days" refund time, a WhatsApp number and an email address, and told a customer an opened, torn bag can't be returned. The agent that reads the policy resource on every model call got all 8 right for 134 more tokens per request at the same latency. Both missed r09 (glass in a drink) on the tool check: the expected escalation call was not made as scored.
production: Re-run whenever the server's tools, descriptions or resources change.
